zh: 一次变换把非对角元素 (r,c) 移到 (c, n−1−r)，两条对角线不动。顺时针转四次就回到原样，所以 turns 很大也只需要做 turns mod 4 次。
非对角位置会分成互不相交的四元轨道：(r,c) → (c,n−1−r) → (n−1−r,n−1−c) → (n−1−c,r) → 回到 (r,c)。每个轨道恰好有一个位置落在顶部严格三角 r < c < n−1−r 里，可以用它当代表，轨道之间互不影响。
读入 n、turns 和整个矩阵（只存一份 32 位整数数组），令 k = turns mod 4。做 k 轮：枚举 r 从 0 到 n/2−1、c 从 r+1 到 n−2−r，用一个临时变量把四个位置的值沿顺时针方向依次挪一格。最后按行输出 n 行。n=1 或 n=2 时没有非对角轨道，矩阵不变；读 INT_MIN 时注意不要在 32 位里溢出。
en: One transformation moves an off-diagonal element (r,c) to (c, n−1−r), and both diagonals stay put. Four clockwise turns restore the original, so even a huge turns only needs turns mod 4 rounds.

The off-diagonal positions split into disjoint four-element orbits: (r,c) → (c,n−1−r) → (n−1−r,n−1−c) → (n−1−c,r) → back to (r,c). Each orbit has exactly one position in the strict top triangle r < c < n−1−r, which can serve as its representative, and orbits do not affect one another.

Read n, turns and the whole matrix (keep just one array of 32-bit integers), and let k = turns mod 4. Do k rounds: for r from 0 to n/2−1 and c from r+1 to n−2−r, use one temporary to move the four values one step clockwise around their orbit. Finally print the n rows. For n=1 or n=2 there are no off-diagonal orbits and the matrix is unchanged; when reading INT_MIN, avoid overflowing 32 bits.

explanationEn:
## Original rules, images and input adaptation

The pinned fastprep/Capital One/capitalone-rotate-matrix-over-diagonals.md defines a square matrix where the elements on the two main diagonals stay in place and the other four triangular regions swap places clockwise. The original asks the reader to look at a source image, but the diagram in the pinned snapshot is an inaccessible local path. This site personally checked the two Problem Source images publicly shown on the original FastPrep page: the first explicitly shows that both diagonals stay fixed and marks the original 5×5 matrix, and the second repeats the rule; neither contains numeric constraints or a picture after rotation. The separately downloaded images are stored at content/oa-judge/source-images/capitalone-18-original-0.jpg and -1.jpg, with hashes bound in the source evidence; these downloaded images must not be claimed to belong to the pinned Git snapshot.

One transformation is exactly: if r=c or r+c=n−1 the element stays; otherwise the original (r,c) moves to (c,n−1−r), that is, a clockwise 90-degree turn. This mapping reproduces, entry by entry, the complete output of the original 5×5 example in the pinned text; it is not a geometric rule added from imagination. It holds for even orders too: for n=2 every position lies on a diagonal, so the matrix never changes; for odd orders the center stays fixed.

The original has no numeric bounds. This site openly adopts the full type ranges of the original Java int[][] and int parameters: elements −2147483648..2147483647, turns as a non-negative count 0..2147483647, and a non-empty square matrix n≥1. Negative counts and empty matrices are not defined by the original, and this site does not add them as extensions. n gets no invented small cap; it is limited by the existing 32MiB standard-input budget.

The first line of standard input is n turns, followed by n lines of n signed integers each (whitespace-separated, allowing LF/CRLF or EOF right at the end); the output is the transformed matrix as n lines, without n. With the shortest single-digit element encoding, a one-digit turns, and EOF with no trailing newline, the input takes 2n²+digits(n)+2 bytes. So 4095 needs 33538056 bytes and is transferable; 4096 needs 33554438 bytes, exceeding 32MiB. 4095 is a derivation from the protocol budget, not a matrix bound given by the original problem; longer numbers reduce the order that actually fits.

## Approach

Four clockwise rotations return every position to where it started, and both diagonals stay fixed every time, so only turns%4 rounds are needed. The off-diagonal positions split into disjoint four-element orbits. Choose the strict top triangle r<c<n−1−r, which picks exactly one representative from each orbit. The four positions of that representative are (r,c), (c,n−1−r), (n−1−r,n−1−c) and (n−1−c,r). Move the four values clockwise with one temporary variable; the other orbits are handled independently, and no second matrix is needed.

## Proof of correctness

The rotation map R(r,c)=(c,n−1−r) maps the union of the two diagonals onto itself, so it also maps off-diagonal positions to off-diagonal positions. R applied four times is the identity. An off-diagonal position cannot be the center, so there are no orbits of length one or two; every orbit has length exactly 4, with one position in each of the four triangular regions, and the strict top triangle contains a unique representative of each orbit.

The in-place cycle passes the values of each representative and the three positions after it along R once, which is exactly the clockwise transformation of that orbit. Different orbits share no positions, so the processing order does not affect the result; the two diagonals are not part of any cycle, so their values do not change. This proves that one round follows the original rule exactly. Repeating turns%4 rounds is the same as repeating turns rounds, so the final output is correct. For n=1 or 2 there are no off-diagonal orbits, and leaving the matrix unchanged also matches the definition.

## Complexity and full budget

At most three rounds, each visiting O(n²) elements; reading and printing are also O(n²). Only one contiguous int32 matrix is stored, with O(1) extra space; for n=4095 the array takes 67076100 bytes, below 256MiB, and the whole output string is not buffered. Parsing INT_MIN accumulates its absolute value in 64 bits before negating, avoiding signed 32-bit overflow; position products use size_t.

The output is just a permutation of the same set of values, adding or removing no values or signs; the total digit bytes of canonical decimal output are no more than the total digit bytes of the input, with at most one separator per value. Apart from a possible trailing-newline difference, the output is smaller than the input minus its header, so a fully transferable matrix can also be printed; the package configures a 64MiB output allowance. The large tests contain only one instance of order 4095, so that repeated large inputs and large expected outputs do not push the whole package over its limit.

## Independent verification

The small-domain oracle directly computes, for every original coordinate, its target coordinate after the repeated rotations and writes into a new matrix, without copying the reference's in-place swaps over the top triangle. It also checks that the diagonals stay fixed and that four turns are the identity. The 163 unique oracle cases cover signed extremes, odd and even orders, and 0/1/2/3/4/INT_MAX turns; binary matrices of orders 1..3 are exhausted with 0..7 turns. The formal cases keep the original 5×5 example and also include even orders, centers, asymmetric reversed data, mixed positive and negative extremes, every period, and medium-scale random data.

The full order-4095 instance generates asymmetric 0/1 values from a coordinate formula; its expected output is produced row by row by inverting each target coordinate back to its original coordinate and substituting into the formula, neither storing a huge Python integer matrix nor calling the reference algorithm. The three wrong programs respectively rotate the diagonals, rotate counterclockwise, and use a period of 2 by mistake; each must exit normally on all formal cases to count as killed.
